# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

### Nov 3, 2026
1 8:37a ○ Scheduler.run_all sleeps after every job, including the last
2 " ● run_all no longer sleeps after the final job
S2 Make run_all sleep only between jobs, then investigate how exceptions in scheduled jobs affect run_pending (Nov 3, 8:37 AM)
S1 Make the scheduler's run_all sleep only between jobs, not after the last one (Nov 3, 8:37 AM)
3 " ○ Scheduler job execution paths and CancelJob handling
S3 Make run_all sleep only between jobs, then plan a fix for exception handling in scheduled jobs (Nov 3, 8:37 AM)
4 8:41a ● run_pending now runs all due jobs when one raises, then re-raises the first exception
5 " ● Job.run reschedules failing jobs via try/finally so they stop re-running every tick
6 " ✓ Added four regression tests for run_all sleep placement and run_pending failure handling
7 " ● Replaced wall-clock sleep in run_pending failure-ordering test with forced past next_run
8 " ○ Full test_schedule.py suite passes with run_pending, Job.run, and run_all changes
9 " ✓ Exception-handling docs now describe run_pending's per-job isolation and rescheduling
S4 Pick up the failing-jobs change in run_pending: keep one failing scheduled job from stopping the other due jobs in the same tick (Nov 3, 8:41 AM)
**Investigated**: Traced Scheduler.run_pending, run_all, _run_job, and Job.run in schedule/__init__.py, plus the existing exception-handling docs and the test layout in test_schedule.py. Confirmed that an exception in Job.run skipped last_run and _schedule_next_run, which left the failed job due.

**Learned**: Before the change, an exception in one due job stopped the sorted loop in run_pending, so later due jobs did not run in that tick. Because the failed job was never rescheduled, it stayed due and re-ran on every run_pending call, which could starve jobs sorted after it. run_all has no exception handling and still stops at the first failure.

**Completed**: run_pending now wraps each job in try/except Exception, runs every due job, re-raises the first exception after the loop, and logs later ones with logger.exception. Job.run now updates last_run and calls _schedule_next_run in a finally block, so failed jobs are rescheduled. run_all sleeps only between jobs. Four new tests were added covering remaining jobs running after a failure, failed-job rescheduling, extra failures being logged, and the run_all sleep count. The failure-ordering test was changed to force past next_run values instead of relying on wall-clock sleeps. The full suite passes at 85 tests, up from 81. docs/exception-handling.rst was updated to describe the new behavior. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: The run_pending and Job.run changes are in place and tested. Possible next work: decide whether run_all should get the same per-job isolation, and check whether _schedule_next_run raising inside the finally block should be guarded so it does not mask the job's original exception.

**Notes**: Behavior change: a job that raises is now rescheduled where it previously stayed due and retried on the next tick. Anyone depending on retry-on-failure would notice. Only the first exception is re-raised, not bundled. Bundling would need ExceptionGroup, which is unavailable on older supported Pythons. A failed job that is past its until() deadline is cancelled on the next tick, not immediately, because the overdue check after execution is skipped when job_func raises.
